A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 30-page OrthoReg paper, including Appendices A–J. Complete text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its associated link.

before.justification: v1 reports original task-addition and task-negation experiments in Section 5, computational-cost measurements in Appendix H.2, and supplementary experiments and LoRA ablations in Appendix J.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices H.2 and J, including accuracy comparisons, computational-cost measurements, and LoRA ablations.

M1.justification: OrthoReg's fine-tuning objective and orthogonality penalty in Equations (7)–(8), its application to weight updates, and the task-vector procedures are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate task addition and negation on Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, GTSRB, MNIST, RESISC45, SUN397, and SVHN, with ImageNet as the negation control task. Appendix coverage is also identical.

E2.justification: The same comparisons retain zero-shot, Non-linear Fine-tuning, Tangent Task Arithmetic, Attention-Only Fine-tuning, and LoRA-ATT. Comparator membership in the computational-cost comparison and LoRA-module ablations also matches.

E3.justification: The three CLIP ViT architectures, evaluation metrics, scaling-coefficient grid search, and experimental procedures are unchanged. The 95%, 90%, and 80% ImageNet-retention thresholds in Tables 2, 4, and 5 are identical.

E4.justification: Both versions retain identical orthogonality analyses, task-vector similarity heatmaps, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, and LoRA-module ablations in Sections 5.4–5.5 and Appendix J.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including the single-run computational-cost measurement described in Appendix H.2. No run-count information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical tables, plotted results, and reported findings match. For example, Table 1 reports 90.41% absolute accuracy for ATT-FT+OrthoReg on ViT-L-14 in both versions; Appendix Tables 3–6 are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, NTK and task-feature-specialization assumptions, theoretical statements, and derivations are identical, including the detailed proofs and theoretical comparisons in Appendices A–H.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about task-feature specialization, orthogonality, OrthoReg, its connection to TTA, and its empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the feature-overlap limitation in Section 4.3.1 and the discussion of weaker or adverse effects from MLP-only regularization in Appendix J.5.2.

D1.justification: The disclosed model configurations, frozen text encoder, regularization search range, computational-resource measurements, and code-access information are identical. The embedded OrthoReg repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and research positioning are identical, including Section 2's pre-merging classification and the relationship to TTA discussed in Section 4.4 and Appendix H.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 18 Apr 2026 to v2 dated 27 Aug 2026. Manuscript wording, headings, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The updated first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly repositioned. Figures 1–11, Tables 1–6, captions, and body and appendix layouts are identical; pages 2–30 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, methods, proofs, experiments, results, references, and appendices are identical. Updating and slightly repositioning the arXiv version/date stamp provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's overall quality.
